places.title: Tour Eiffel, Champ-de-Mars and Trocadéro
places.architect: Gustave Eiffel, Maurice Koechlin, Émile Nouguier, Stephen Sauvestre (tower); Jacques Carlu, Louis-Hippolyte Boileau, Léon Azéma (Palais de Chaillot)
places.why: The wrought-iron tower of the 1889 World's Fair stands at the end of the long lawn of the Champ-de-Mars and faces the Palais de Chaillot across the Seine. The terrace between Chaillot's two curved wings gives the classic full view of the tower.

photos.file: Paris - The Eiffel Tower in spring - 2307.jpg
photos.author: Jorge Royan

photos.file: Champ de Mars from the Eiffel Tower - July 2006 edit.jpg
photos.author: Diliff , edited by Fir0002

places.title: Palais du Louvre and Jardin des Tuileries
places.architect: Pierre Lescot, Claude Perrault, Louis Visconti, Hector Lefuel; I. M. Pei (pyramid); André Le Nôtre (garden)
places.why: Eight centuries of royal building around the Cour Carrée and the Cour Napoléon, where Pei's glass pyramid became the museum entrance in 1989. West of the palace, Le Nôtre's formal garden runs through the Tuileries to the Place de la Concorde.

photos.file: Arc de triomphe du carrousel in Paris France.jpg
photos.author: Tim Adams

places.title: Place de la Concorde
places.why: The largest square in Paris, laid out for Louis XV between the Tuileries and the Champs-Élysées, with the Luxor obelisk at its centre and two cast-iron fountains. Gabriel's twin palaces close the north side; one of them, the Hôtel de la Marine, is open to visitors.

photos.file: Fountain of the Seas, Paris 16 August 2014.jpg
photos.author: Benh LIEU SONG from Torcy, France

places.title: Avenue des Champs-Élysées and Arc de Triomphe
places.why: Two kilometres of avenue rising from the Concorde to the Arc de Triomphe, which stands at the centre of a star of twelve avenues. The roof terrace of the arch looks down the whole historic axis, from the Louvre to La Défense.

photos.file: Paris - arc de triomphe de l'Étoile - 2026-09-16 14-34-17 010.jpg
photos.author: Matthias_Süßen

photos.file: Avenue des Champs-Elysées from top of Arc de triomphe Paris.jpg
photos.author: Jebulon

photos.file: Le Départ des Volontaires (La Marseillaise) par Rude, Arc de Triomphe Etoile Paris.jpg
photos.author: Jebulon

places.title: Île de la Cité, Notre-Dame and Île Saint-Louis
places.architect: Maurice de Sully (Notre-Dame); Eugène Viollet-le-Duc (19th-century restoration)
places.why: The island where Paris began, with the Gothic cathedral of Notre-Dame, the royal palace of the Conciergerie and the Pont Neuf, the oldest bridge in the city. Next door, the quieter Île Saint-Louis keeps its 17th-century streets and quays almost intact.

places.title: Sainte-Chapelle
places.why: A royal chapel built to hold relics of the Passion. Its upper chapel is almost entirely walls of 13th-century stained glass, fifteen metres high.

photos.file: Santa Capilla, París, Francia, 2022-11-01, DD 80-82 HDR.jpg
photos.author: Diego Delso

photos.file: Santa Capilla, París, Francia, 2022-11-01, DD 50-52 HDR.jpg
photos.author: Diego Delso

places.title: Montmartre and the Sacré-Cœur
places.why: The hill village of painters and cabarets, with steep lanes and stairways around the Place du Tertre. On the summit, the white domes of the Sacré-Cœur overlook the whole city from its highest point.

photos.file: Paris - Basilique du Sacré-Cœur de Montmartre - 2025-09-30 23-31-57 001.jpg
photos.author: Giò Terra ( Terragio67 )

places.title: Le Marais
places.why: The old aristocratic quarter that escaped Haussmann's rebuilding: narrow streets of 17th-century town houses around hidden courtyards, several of them now museums, with the Hôtel de Ville at its edge.

photos.file: Paris - Hôtel de ville de Paris - vue du pont Saint Louis - 2025-10-12 07-51-32 001.jpg
photos.author: Terragio67

places.title: Place des Vosges
places.why: The oldest planned square in Paris: 36 brick-and-stone houses of the same design over a continuous arcade, around a garden of lime trees and fountains.

photos.file: Plaza de los Vosgos, París, Francia, 2022-10-30, DD 58.jpg
photos.author: Diego Delso

photos.file: F0723 Paris IV place Vosges statue Louis XIII rwk.jpg
photos.author: Mbzt

places.title: Quartier latin and the Panthéon
places.why: The university quarter of the left bank, with the Sorbonne, medieval churches, the Roman arena of Lutetia and the Panthéon, Soufflot's domed church turned into the resting place of France's great figures.

photos.file: Chapelle Sainte-Ursule de la Sorbonne, Paris 001.jpg
photos.author: Moonik

places.title: Saint-Germain-des-Prés
places.why: The left-bank quarter of cafés, bookshops and galleries around the Romanesque bell tower of Saint-Germain-des-Prés, the oldest church in Paris, with the vast classical church of Saint-Sulpice a few streets south.
places.note: The outline is the administrative quarter of Saint-Germain-des-Prés.

photos.file: Abadía de Saint-Germain-des-Prés, París, Francia, 2022-11-01, DD 12.jpg
photos.author: Diego Delso

photos.file: Abadía de Saint-Germain-des-Prés, París, Francia, 2022-11-01, DD 23-25 HDR.jpg
photos.author: Diego Delso

places.title: Jardin du Luxembourg
places.why: The garden of the Luxembourg Palace, now the Senate: terraces around an octagonal pond, the Medici Fountain, statues and the free green chairs that all of Paris uses.

photos.author: Benh LIEU SONG , crane cloned out by Sanchezn

photos.file: Paris Palais du Luxembourg façade s printemps 2014.jpg
photos.author: JLPC

photos.file: Paris Jardin Luxembourg Polyphème surprenant A&G 2014.jpg
photos.author: JLPC

places.title: Palais Garnier
places.why: Napoleon III's opera house and the showpiece of Second Empire Paris, with a polychrome facade, a marble grand staircase and a gilded foyer as rich as a palace.

photos.author: Photograph: Eric Pouhier , Modifier: Rainer Zenz , Niabot (last modification)

places.title: Grand Palais, Petit Palais and Pont Alexandre-III
places.architect: Charles Girault, Henri Deglane, Albert Louvet, Albert Thomas; Jean Résal (bridge)
places.why: Three works of the 1900 World's Fair: the Grand Palais with its huge nave of glass and steel, the Petit Palais opposite, and the Pont Alexandre-III, the most ornate bridge in Paris, leading across to the Invalides.

photos.file: Harmony triumphing over Discord Quadriga Récipon Grand Palais Paris.jpg
photos.author: Jebulon

places.title: Les Invalides
places.why: Louis XIV's hospital for old soldiers, a long classical front behind a vast lawn, crowned by the gilded dome of the royal church where Napoleon lies.

photos.file: Hôtel des Invalides, North View, Paris 7e 140402 1.jpg
photos.author: DXR

photos.file: Sarcófago de Napoleón Bonaparte, cúpula de los Inválidos, París, Francia, 2022-10-30, DD 89-91 HDR.jpg
photos.author: Diego Delso

places.title: Parc Rives de Seine
places.why: Former riverside expressways turned into a promenade on both banks of the Seine, below the city's great monuments. Locals walk, run, cycle and picnic along the water.

photos.file: Parc Rives de Seine @ Seine @ Paris (33693882194).jpg
photos.author: Guilhem Vellut from Paris, France

photos.file: Parc Rives de Seine @ Pont Alexandre III @ Paris (33975157210).jpg
photos.author: Guilhem Vellut from Paris, France

places.title: Canal Saint-Martin and Bassin de la Villette
places.why: A 19th-century canal of locks, iron footbridges and plane trees, whose quays fill with picnics on summer evenings; to the north it opens onto the wide Bassin de la Villette.

places.title: Cimetière du Père-Lachaise
places.why: A hillside cemetery laid out as a landscape park, with cobbled avenues under old trees and thousands of chapels and sculpted tombs of the famous.

places.title: Centre Pompidou
places.architect: Renzo Piano, Richard Rogers, Gianfranco Franchini
places.why: The building that turned architecture inside out: structure, pipes and escalators in colour-coded steel on the facades, leaving the floors free inside, and a sloping piazza in front that works as a public square.

places.title: Tour Montparnasse
places.architect: Eugène Beaudouin, Urbain Cassan, Louis de Hoÿm de Marien, Jean Saubot
places.why: The only skyscraper in central Paris, much criticised when it went up. Its top-floor terrace gives a view of the whole city, the Eiffel Tower included.

places.title: Musée d'Orsay
places.architect: Victor Laloux; ACT Architecture and Gae Aulenti (museum)
places.why: A Beaux-Arts railway station of 1900 on the Seine, converted into the museum of 19th-century art. Its great barrel-vaulted hall and station clocks were kept.

photos.file: Musee d'Orsay and Pont Royal, North-West view 140402 1.jpg
photos.author: DXR

places.title: Basilique Saint-Denis
places.why: The abbey church where Gothic architecture was born, with the first choir of pointed vaults and wide windows, and the burial place of the kings of France with their sculpted tombs.

photos.file: Basilique St Denis façade ouest St Denis Seine St Denis 20.jpg
photos.author: Chabe01

photos.file: Basilique Saint-Denis Louis XII Anne de Bretagne tombeau.jpg
photos.author: Myrabella

photos.file: Basilica of Saint Denis North Transept Rose Window, Paris, France - Diliff.jpg
photos.author: Diliff

places.title: Château and Parc de Versailles
places.architect: Louis Le Vau, Jules Hardouin-Mansart; André Le Nôtre (gardens)
places.why: Louis XIV's palace and the model for royal residences across Europe, with the Hall of Mirrors and formal gardens of terraces, fountains and a cross-shaped canal stretching to the horizon.

photos.file: Main Façade, Palace of Versailles, Cour Royale.jpg
photos.author: Julian Lupyan

places.title: Tour Saint-Jacques
places.why: The Flamboyant Gothic bell tower of a church demolished after the Revolution, standing alone in a small square; it marked a starting point of the pilgrims' way to Santiago.

photos.file: Tour Saint-Jacques and Fontaine du Palmier, South-East View 140207 1.jpg
photos.author: DXR

places.title: Hôtel de Cluny and Thermes de Cluny
places.why: A late-Gothic town house of the abbots of Cluny built against the ruins of Roman baths, whose vaulted cold room still stands. It houses the museum of the Middle Ages.

places.title: Hôtel Salé — Musée Picasso
places.why: One of the grandest Baroque town houses of the Marais, with a sculpted grand staircase, converted into the Picasso museum by Roland Simounet.

places.title: Hôtel Biron — Musée Rodin
places.why: A rococo mansion where Rodin lived and worked, with his sculptures set among the roses and clipped trees of the garden behind the house.

photos.file: L'hôtel Biron (musée Rodin) à Paris, 13 juin 2021 01.jpg
photos.author: Jean-Pierre Dalbéra

places.title: Galeries Lafayette and Printemps Haussmann
places.architect: Georges Chedanne, Ferdinand Chanut (Galeries Lafayette); Paul Sédille, René Binet (Printemps)
places.why: Two department stores of the Belle Époque on the Boulevard Haussmann: the Galeries Lafayette under a stained-glass Art Nouveau dome, and the Printemps with its corner domes and mosaic facades. Both have roof terraces over the Opéra quarter.

photos.file: Printemps viewed from Opéra Garnier's roof.jpg
photos.author: FR

places.title: Passages couverts
places.why: Glass-roofed shopping arcades of the early 19th century with mosaic floors, carved shopfronts and old bookshops, forerunners of the department store; several can be walked one after another.

places.title: Grande Mosquée de Paris
places.architect: Maurice Tranchant de Lunel, Robert Fournez, Maurice Mantout, Charles Heubès
places.why: A Hispano-Moorish mosque with a 33-metre minaret, built to honour the Muslim soldiers of the First World War. Its tiled patio garden and tea room are open to visitors.

places.title: La Samaritaine
places.architect: Frantz Jourdain, Henri Sauvage; SANAA (2021 renovation)
places.why: A department store by the Pont Neuf with an Art Nouveau hall of iron and painted glass and an Art Deco front on the Seine, restored in 2021 with a new undulating glass facade on the rue de Rivoli.

places.title: Théâtre des Champs-Élysées
places.architect: Auguste Perret; Henry van de Velde (early design); Antoine Bourdelle (reliefs)
places.why: One of the first public buildings in reinforced concrete, a sober white facade carved with Bourdelle's marble reliefs, where The Rite of Spring premiered in 1913.

places.title: Palais de la Porte Dorée
places.why: Built for the 1931 Colonial Exhibition, an Art Deco palace wrapped in a vast carved stone relief, with period interiors. It now houses the museum of immigration and a tropical aquarium.

places.title: Piscine Molitor
places.why: An Art Deco swimming complex styled like an ocean liner, with yellow galleries of cabins around an outdoor and an indoor pool. It reopened in 2014 as part of a hotel.

places.title: Église de la Madeleine
places.why: A church in the form of a Greek temple, ringed by 52 Corinthian columns, closing the axis of the Rue Royale opposite the National Assembly across the Concorde.

places.title: Place Vendôme
places.why: An octagonal royal square of uniform facades, now home to jewellers and the Ritz, around a column clad in bronze from cannons captured at Austerlitz.

places.title: Église Saint-Eustache
places.why: A church with the plan and height of a Gothic cathedral dressed in Renaissance detail, rising over the Les Halles garden, with one of the largest organs in France.

photos.file: Iglesia de San Eustaquio, París, Francia, 2022-10-31, DD 133-135 HDR.jpg
photos.author: Diego Delso

places.title: Porte Saint-Denis and Porte Saint-Martin
places.why: Two triumphal arches built for Louis XIV on the line of the demolished city walls, where the Grands Boulevards begin.

places.title: Place de la Bastille and Opéra Bastille
places.architect: Jean-Antoine Alavoine, Joseph-Louis Duc (column); Carlos Ott (opera)
places.why: The square of the demolished prison, with the bronze July Column topped by the gilded Spirit of Freedom, the glass Opéra Bastille on one side and the Arsenal marina on the other.

places.title: Philharmonie de Paris and Cité de la musique
places.architect: Ateliers Jean Nouvel (Philharmonie); Christian de Portzamparc (Cité de la musique)
places.why: Two music buildings at the edge of the Parc de la Villette: Portzamparc's Cité de la musique, a village of geometric volumes along an inner street, and Nouvel's Philharmonie, a hill clad in aluminium bird patterns with a public path to its roof.

places.title: Institut du monde arabe
places.why: A glass and steel box on the Seine whose south facade is made of hundreds of metal diaphragms, a modern mashrabiya designed to open and close with the light. The roof terrace looks over Notre-Dame.

places.title: Bibliothèque nationale de France — François-Mitterrand
places.why: Four glass towers shaped like open books at the corners of a vast timber esplanade around a sunken forest garden. The Simone-de-Beauvoir footbridge links it across the Seine to Bercy.

places.title: Fondation Louis Vuitton
places.why: Twelve curved glass sails over a white iceberg of panels at the edge of the Bois de Boulogne, with roof terraces at several levels open to visitors.

places.title: Bourse de Commerce — Pinault Collection
places.architect: Nicolas Le Camus de Mézières; Henri Blondel; Tadao Ando (museum)
places.why: A round 18th-century grain exchange under a dome of glass and iron, into which Tadao Ando set a concrete cylinder to make a museum of contemporary art.

photos.file: Paris 1er - Bourse de commerce - Portique - Fronton (Aristide Croisy).jpg
photos.author: Romainbehar

places.title: Palais de Tokyo
places.architect: Jean-Claude Dondel, André Aubert, Paul Viard, Marcel Dastugue; Lacaton & Vassal (conversion)
places.why: A monumental exhibition palace of 1937 on the Seine. Lacaton & Vassal stripped its west wing back to raw concrete to make one of the largest contemporary art centres in Europe; the east wing holds the city's museum of modern art.

places.title: Musée du quai Branly — Jacques Chirac
places.architect: Ateliers Jean Nouvel; Patrick Blanc (green wall); Gilles Clément (garden)
places.why: A long museum on stilts above a wild garden, hidden from the quay behind a glass screen, next to an office block covered by Patrick Blanc's vertical garden.

places.title: La Seine Musicale
places.why: A music centre on the tip of the island where the Renault factory stood: a woven timber egg for the auditorium, a sail of solar panels that turns with the sun and a roof garden open to all.

places.title: Fondation Jérôme Seydoux-Pathé
places.why: A curved shell of aluminium louvres rising from a courtyard behind a 19th-century theatre facade carved by the young Rodin, home of the Pathé film foundation.

places.title: Les Docks — Cité de la Mode et du Design
places.why: Concrete warehouses of 1907 on the Seine wrapped in an acid-green glass tube that carries ramps up to a roof terrace over the river.

places.title: La Canopée des Halles
places.why: An undulating roof of yellow glass louvres over the entrance to the Forum des Halles, the underground hub on the site of the old central market, opening onto a new garden.

places.title: Le Monde Group headquarters
places.why: A bridge-building that spans a public square over the tracks of the Gare d'Austerlitz, its facade made of thousands of glass pixels.

places.title: Tribunal de Paris
places.why: The new Paris law courts: a 160-metre tower of stacked glass blocks set back in steps, with trees planted on each terrace, at the edge of the Batignolles district.

places.title: Fondation Cartier building, boulevard Raspail
places.why: A building of layered glass screens set in front of and behind a wild garden, so that trees, sky and reflections blur the edge between inside and out.
places.note: The Fondation Cartier moved to Place du Palais-Royal in 2025.

places.title: Cinémathèque française
places.why: Gehry's first building in Paris, built as the American Center: a cascade of tilted and twisted limestone volumes facing the Parc de Bercy.

places.title: Hôtel industriel Berlier
places.why: Perrault's first major work by the ring road: a pure prism of clear glass over concrete floors, built as a vertical industrial estate for light workshops.

places.title: Poste du Louvre
places.why: The central post office of Paris, a block-sized building on an iron frame, opened up by Perrault with passages to a new courtyard and a mix of uses, while the post office still works on the ground floor.

places.title: Morland Mixité Capitale
places.why: A 1950s government office block on the Seine converted into a mix of housing, hotel, youth hostel, market and offices, with a rooftop open to the public.

places.title: Villa Savoye
places.why: Le Corbusier's manifesto house: a white box on slender pilotis with a ribbon window, a roof garden and a ramp that leads up through the house, set in a meadow.

places.title: Maisons La Roche and Jeanneret
places.why: Two joined houses at the end of a cul-de-sac, one built as a gallery for a collector with a curved picture gallery and a ramp. They house the Fondation Le Corbusier.

places.title: Cité de Refuge de l'Armée du Salut
places.why: A Salvation Army hostel with a long glazed front and a colourful entrance sequence of pavilion, bridge and rotunda, one of Le Corbusier's first large buildings.

places.title: Cité internationale universitaire de Paris
places.architect: Le Corbusier (Fondation suisse; Maison du Brésil with Lúcio Costa); Bruther (Maison Julie-Victoire Daubié)
places.why: A campus park of about forty student houses, each built by a country in its own style, among them Le Corbusier's Swiss and Brazilian pavilions and Bruther's glass-and-concrete residence for researchers.

places.title: La Défense
places.architect: Johan Otto von Spreckelsen, Paul Andreu (Grande Arche); Robert Camelot, Jean de Mailly, Bernard Zehrfuss, Nicolas Esquillan (CNIT)
places.why: Europe's largest business district, a pedestrian deck over roads and railways lined with towers. The Grande Arche, a hollow cube 110 metres high, closes the historic axis from the Louvre, and the concrete shell of the CNIT rests on just three points.

places.title: Mémorial des Martyrs de la Déportation
places.why: A crypt at the tip of the Île de la Cité, reached by a narrow stair down to the water, with a barred opening onto the Seine and a gallery lit by thousands of glass points in memory of the deported.

places.title: Siège du Parti communiste français
places.why: A curved slab of glass over a white concrete dome that rises from the forecourt like a half-buried sphere, containing the party's council chamber.

places.title: Les Orgues de Flandre
places.why: Housing towers and slabs of staggered concrete volumes, named after musical forms, whose serrated silhouettes recall organ pipes.

places.title: Les Choux de Créteil
places.why: Ten round housing towers whose balconies curve out like the leaves of a cabbage, the best-known image of the new towns of the 1970s.

places.title: Espaces d'Abraxas and Arènes de Picasso
places.architect: Ricardo Bofill, Taller de Arquitectura (Abraxas); Manuel Núñez Yanowsky (Arènes de Picasso)
places.why: Two monumental housing estates of the new town of Marne-la-Vallée: Bofill's theatre, palace and arch of prefabricated classical concrete, and the Arènes de Picasso with their two giant discs.

places.title: Tours Aillaud (Tours Nuages)
places.why: Eighteen rounded towers wrapped in mosaic in cloud and sky colours, with round, square and drop-shaped windows scattered over their facades.

places.title: Bourse départementale du travail
places.why: A trade-union house by Niemeyer: a slim concrete office slab beside a sweeping curved auditorium.

places.title: UNESCO headquarters
places.architect: Marcel Breuer, Pier Luigi Nervi, Bernard Zehrfuss; Tadao Ando (meditation space)
places.why: A Y-shaped concrete building on pilotis with a folded conference hall by Nervi, a Japanese garden by Isamu Noguchi and a small meditation pavilion by Tadao Ando.

places.title: Maison de Verre
places.why: A doctor's house and surgery built with a facade of glass blocks, a steel frame and machine-like fittings, an icon of modernism tucked into a courtyard.
places.note: Private house in a courtyard; the glass-block facade is seen only through the entrance gate.

places.title: Immeuble Molitor
places.why: An apartment building with facades of glass and glass blocks on both sides, where Le Corbusier lived in the top-floor apartment and studio.

places.title: Rue Mallet-Stevens
places.why: A private street of white cubist villas built by one architect for artists and friends, with interlocking volumes, terraces and a tower-like staircase.

photos.file: Villa des frères Martel construite par Robert Mallet-Stevens au 10 rue Mallet-Stevens (Paris), en 1927.jpg
photos.author: Rory Hide ( https://www.flickr.com/people/roryrory/ )

places.title: Hector Guimard in Auteuil
places.why: Art Nouveau houses by the designer of the metro entrances, with twisting ironwork, carved stone and asymmetric bays: the Castel Béranger, his own Hôtel Guimard and the Hôtel Mezzara.

photos.file: Lentrée du bâtiment arrière du Castel Béranger (Hector Guimard) (5478786063).jpg
photos.author: Jean-Pierre Dalbéra from Paris, France

places.title: Immeuble Lavirotte
places.why: One of the most extravagant Art Nouveau facades in Paris, with glazed ceramics and sculpted figures, animals and plants around a carved wooden door.

places.title: 25 bis rue Franklin
places.architect: Auguste and Gustave Perret; Alexandre Bigot (ceramics)
places.why: One of the first apartment buildings to show its reinforced-concrete frame, which the Perret brothers clad in ceramic leaves, with the front opened into a U for more light.

photos.file: 25 bis Rue Benjamin Franklin 2, Paris, France 2010.jpg
photos.author: seier+seier

places.title: Tour Bois-le-Prêtre
places.architect: Raymond Lopez (1961); Frédéric Druot, Lacaton & Vassal (transformation)
places.why: A 1960s social housing tower that was wrapped in a new skin of winter gardens and balconies instead of being demolished, while its tenants stayed at home.

places.title: Housing on rue des Suisses
places.why: Social housing set inside a Paris block, with folding cast-iron shutters on the street fronts and low houses behind covered in wooden roller blinds around a planted courtyard.

places.title: Housing at 64 rue de Meaux
places.why: Social housing around a garden courtyard planted with birches, with facades of terracotta panels fixed on a fine prefabricated frame.

places.title: Cité-jardin de la Butte-Rouge
places.architect: Joseph Bassompierre, Paul de Rutté, André Arfvidson, Paul Sirvin
places.why: A garden city of pink rendered housing blocks set among woods and lawns, built in stages over thirty years for working families.

places.title: Butte-aux-Cailles
places.why: A village of low houses and cobbled lanes on a small hill, with street art and bars, and a brick swimming pool of 1924 fed by an artesian well.

photos.file: F1813 Paris XIII place Paul-Verlaine piscine butte Cailles rwk.jpg
photos.author: Mbzt

places.title: Clichy-Batignolles and Parc Martin-Luther-King
places.why: A new eco-district on former rail yards, with housing blocks by many architects around a ten-hectare park of lawns, wetlands and sports grounds.

places.title: Ivry-sur-Seine town centre
places.why: A town centre rebuilt without right angles: star-shaped concrete buildings with planted terraces on every level, mixing flats, shops and gardens.

places.title: Maison de Tristan Tzara
places.why: The only building in Paris by Adolf Loos, a house for the Dada poet set into the slope of Montmartre: a rubble-stone base and a smooth white upper block cut by a deep loggia.

photos.file: Paris, France, House of Tristan Tzara (Avenue Junot).jpg
photos.author: Britchi Mirela

places.title: Jardin du Palais-Royal
places.why: A quiet garden of clipped lime trees enclosed by arcades of shops and cafés, entered through a courtyard of Buren's striped columns.

photos.file: P1120936 Paris Ier Palais-Royal galerie de Beaujolais rwk.JPG
photos.author: Mbzt

places.title: Parc des Buttes-Chaumont
places.why: A former quarry turned into a picturesque park with steep lawns, a lake and a temple on a rocky island, the favourite of north-east Paris on summer evenings.

photos.file: Parc Buttes Chaumont vu depuis Rue Botzaris - Paris XIX (FR75) - 2021-03-06 - 7.jpg
photos.author: Chabe01

photos.file: Overview of Parc des Buttes-Chaumont, Paris 19e 140427 1.jpg
photos.author: DXR

places.title: Parc de la Villette
places.why: One of the largest parks in Paris, on the site of the old slaughterhouses: lawns, themed gardens and red steel follies on a grid, around the 19th-century Grande Halle and the mirrored sphere of the Géode.

places.title: Jardin des Plantes
places.why: The botanical garden of the Natural History Museum, with formal flower beds, iron-and-glass greenhouses of the 1830s, a small zoo and the Grande Galerie de l'Évolution.

photos.file: 2004.04.16 Photo 039 Paris 5e jardin des plantes encours.jpg
photos.author: Mbzt

photos.file: Carré Descaine Jardin Plantes - Paris V (FR75) - 2021-07-30 - 3.jpg
photos.author: Chabe01

places.title: Parc André-Citroën
places.architect: Gilles Clément, Alain Provost, Patrick Berger, Jean-Paul Viguier, Jean-François Jodry
places.why: A park on the site of the Citroën car plant: a great lawn sloping to the Seine between two glass greenhouses, with gardens of colours and a wild garden.

places.title: Parc Monceau
places.why: An 18th-century landscape garden with follies, a colonnade around an oval pond and gilded gates, surrounded by the mansions of the Plaine Monceau.

places.title: Parc Montsouris
places.why: A rolling landscape park at the southern edge of Paris with a lake, a waterfall and old trees, crossed by the old Petite Ceinture railway in a cutting.

places.title: Parc Georges-Brassens
places.why: A park on the site of the old horse market that kept the auction hall and its belfry, with a small vineyard, a scented garden and a weekend book market under the old halls.

photos.file: Central building of Parc Georges-Brassens, Paris 15e 20140213 1.jpg
photos.author: DXR

places.title: Parc de Belleville
places.why: A terraced park down the slope of Belleville with a long cascade and, at the top, a belvedere with one of the widest views over Paris.

places.title: Bois de Vincennes, Parc Floral and Château de Vincennes
places.why: The largest green space of Paris, a wooded park with lakes and boating, the gardens of the Parc Floral, and the royal castle of Vincennes with the tallest medieval keep in Europe.

photos.file: Lac Daumesnil @ Bois de Vincennes @ Paris (23620282050).jpg
photos.author: Guilhem Vellut from Paris, France

places.title: Bois de Boulogne and Parc de Bagatelle
places.why: The western wooded park laid out for Napoleon III with lakes, islands and an artificial waterfall. Inside it, the small château and rose garden of Bagatelle make one of the prettiest gardens in Paris.

photos.file: Lac inférieur du bois de Boulogne, Paris 12.jpg
photos.author: Polymagou

photos.file: Grande cascade du bois de Boulogne.jpg
photos.author: LPLT

photos.file: Kiosque de l'Empereur Bois de Boulogne Paris 16e 002.jpg
photos.author: Moonik

places.title: Jardin des Serres d'Auteuil
places.why: A botanical garden of iron-and-glass greenhouses around a formal parterre, with a domed palm house and tropical plants.

places.title: Coulée verte René-Dumont and Viaduc des Arts
places.architect: Jacques Vergely, Philippe Mathieux (promenade); Patrick Berger (viaduct arches)
places.why: The first elevated park in the world, on a disused railway: a planted walk on top of a brick viaduct whose arches hold craft workshops, continuing east through gardens and tunnels towards the Bois de Vincennes.

places.title: Place de la République
places.architect: TVK (2013 redesign); Léopold and Charles Morice (monument)
places.why: A square freed from traffic in 2013 and paved as one large pedestrian space around the Monument to the Republic, with a café, a fountain and room for skaters and gatherings.

photos.file: Paris 3e - Place de la République - Monument à la République 01.jpg
photos.author: Romainbehar

places.title: Grand Parc des Docks de Saint-Ouen
places.why: A new park by the Seine at the heart of the Docks district, with meadows, allotments, a greenhouse and rain gardens that collect and clean the district's run-off.

places.title: Parc de Sceaux
places.why: Le Nôtre's landscape for Colbert, with a grand canal, a cascade of fountains and long lines of trees around a 19th-century château.
